items.label: text
items.text: To find the mass of Fe we multiply the number of moles of Fe by the mass of 1 mole of Fe (56 g). A common mistake is to multiply the number of moles by the mass of 2Fe (112 g), but we have already used the '2' when we worked out the number of moles of Fe.

items.label: section_header
items.text: A PROBLEM ABOUT EXTRACTING IRON

items.label: text
items.text: The equation below is for a reaction that occurs in the extraction of iron:

items.label: formula
items.text: F e _ { 2 } O _ { 3 } + 3 C \rightarrow 2 F e + 3 C O

items.label: text
items.text: Calculate the mass of iron which can be formed from 1000g of iron oxide.

items.label: text
items.text: We are given the mass of Fe2O₃ in the question and so we can calculate the number of moles of Fe2O3:

items.label: formula
items.text: n u m b e r o f m o l e = \frac { \ m a s s } { \ m a s s o f 1 \, m o l e }

items.label: formula
items.text: n u m b e r o f m o i s = \frac { 1 0 0 0 } { 1 6 0 } = 6 . 2 5 m o i

items.label: text
items.text: From the chemical equation we can see that 1 mol Fe2O3 produces 2 mol Fe. We know this because of the big numbers in front of the formulae.

items.label: text
items.text: So we know that, if we start with a certain number of moles of Fe2O3, we will obtain twice as many moles of Fe.

items.label: text
items.text: So 6.25 mol Fe2O3 produces 2 × 6.25 = 12.5 mol Fe:

items.label: text
items.text: mass = number of moles × mass of 1 mole

items.label: text
items.text: The mass of 12.5 mol Fe is 12.5 × 56 = 700 g.
